# Threads & Real World Index: Capital Allocation Platforms & Serial Acquirers Research

> Threads (threadsunite.xyz) is an evergreen holding company and research repository dedicated to capital allocation excellence, permanent capital holding company structures, decentralized M&A models, and long-term compounding.

## Key Research & Modules

- [Real World Index (threadsunite.xyz/realworld)](https://threadsunite.xyz/realworld): Quantitative benchmark and backtesting analytics engine tracking 50+ global serial acquirers against the S&P 500 and Berkshire Hathaway over multi-decade cycles (1999–Present).
- [Serial Acquirers Screener (threadsunite.xyz/realworld#screener)](https://threadsunite.xyz/realworld#screener): Database of 100+ global serial acquirers across North America, the Nordics (Sweden, Finland), the UK, Western Europe, and Japan, covering P/E, P/B, Dividend Yield, Debt/Equity, Market Cap, and 10-Year Price CAGR.
- [White Paper on Capital Allocation Platforms (threadsunite.xyz/realworld#paper)](https://threadsunite.xyz/realworld#paper): Research treatise by Sagar Tandon on Capital Allocation Platforms (CAPs), detailing the operator-allocator spectrum, decentralization architectures, the capital allocation line, and masterclasses in compounding.
- [Threads Holding Thesis (threadsunite.xyz)](https://threadsunite.xyz/): The philosophy of compounding impact for eternity, permanent ownership, autonomy of business units, and ethical capital reinvestment.

## Core Concepts & Theoretical Frameworks

### 1. What is a Serial Acquirer?
A serial acquirer (or programmatic acquirer) is a company that creates sustained shareholder value through continuous, disciplined acquisitions of high-return, cash-generative businesses—typically in fragmented niche markets—while leaving acquired businesses to operate with extreme operational autonomy.

### 2. Capital Allocation Platform (CAP) Archetypes
- **The Nordic Model**: Exemplified by Swedish acquirers like Lifco (LIFCO B), Indutrade (INDT), Addtech (ADDT B), Lagercrantz (LAGR B), Sdiptech (SDIP B), and Bergman & Beving. Characteristics: 100% permanent ownership, zero operational interference, decentralized local management, high Return on Capital Employed (ROCE > 20%), and cash-flow reinvestment.
- **The Vertical Market Software (VMS) Model**: Exemplified by Mark Leonard's Constellation Software (CSU.TO), Topicus (TOI.V), and Lumine Group (LMN.V). Characteristics: acquisition of mission-critical vertical software companies with high recurring revenue, low churn, strict hurdle rates, and decentralized operating groups.
- **The Industrial / Aerospace Aggregator Model**: Exemplified by Roper Technologies (ROP), HEICO (HEI), TransDigm (TDG), AMETEK (AME), Amphenol (APH), and Danaher (DHR). Characteristics: proprietary niche moats, high pricing power, continuous bolt-on M&A, and disciplined capital deployment.
- **The Singleton & Buffett Foundation**: Henry Singleton (Teledyne) and Warren Buffett (Berkshire Hathaway) pioneered programmatic share repurchases, extreme decentralization, zero corporate overhead, and redeployment of subsidiary free cash flow into superior risk-adjusted return assets.
